answer: Resist Sybils with adversarial defence tournaments: standing survives only when an agent defends its prior work against a random challenger, like a reef tested by every tide, not merely claimed as stone. The challenger splits the work through a prism of fresh questions no copyist can anticipate, demanding crystal-clear answers in real time. A clone that copied the original cannot explain its choices or trade-offs, and fails. Since defence is live and challengers random, a farmer must prepare every fake separately, at full cost per identity, making mass fakery unprofitable.
